Guidance & outlook: ICRA expects domestic commercial vehicle wholesale volumes to grow by 4% to 6% in FY27, reflecting a normalization after the strong growth witnessed in FY26.
The share of customers with a CIBIL score above 725 has steadily increased from 63% in FY24 to 79% in FY26 and further to 84% in Q1 FY27.
Moving on to our progress towards FY29 guidance of 35% CAGR growth in disbursements and a target PAT of INR450 crores to INR500 crores.
Growth & demand: Reflecting these challenges, the Reserve Bank of India has revised its FY27 GDP growth forecast to 6.6%.

IndoStar Capital Finance Limited July 30, 2026 Against this backdrop, the Monetary Policy Committee has maintained the repo rate at 5.25%, while retaining a neutral policy stance, reflecting a balanced approach towards supporting growth, while keeping inflation under control.

While the pace of growth is expected to moderate due to higher base, the underlying demand environment remains healthy, supported by continued government infrastructure spending, replacement demand and better affordability following the reduction in GST rates.
Margins & costs: At the same time, retail inflation increased to 4.38% in June from 3.93% in May, largely driven by higher food and fuel prices.
We are still, however, able to manage disbursement yield of about 20% plus besides processing fees and cost to income.
While cost of funds raised this quarter was marginally higher, we expect our overall cost of borrowing to come down over the next couple of quarters as the higher cost debt is repaid.
Capex & expansion: The business continues to operate on a fully digital journey with 100% e-application, e- agreement and e-NACH, while leveraging our existing vehicle finance branch network, allowing us to scale without any incremental branch capex.
This came mainly from NIM expansion to 8.8% from 6.2% a year ago.
Operating expenses were INR129 crores against INR139 crores in Q1 FY26, a reduction of about 7% even as we kept investing in the branches and people.
Balance sheet & cash: On liability side, during the quarter, we raised INR1,220 crores through term loans, NCDs and CPs at a cost of 9.11%, taking our total debt outstanding to around INR5,681 crores.
Debt to equity was at 1.54x, and we continue to maintain a positive ALM position across all maturity buckets.
And our cost of borrowing, as I mentioned, we raised money at around 9%, 9.11% last quarter.
Risks & challenges: While the domestic economy continues to demonstrate resilience, global conflicts, elevated energy prices and weather-related uncertainties remain key risks that could impact both urban and rural demand.
While the non-starter ratio has declined from 3.76% to 1.65% over the same period.
During the quarter, our weighted average cost of funds declined by nearly 80 basis points year-on-year.

Growth & demand: In terms of overarching macro trends, India's real GDP grew at 7.8% in Q1 FY '26, driven by the government's spending on infra rural wage growth and services.

The Reserve Bank of India has revised its GDP growth forecast for FY '26 to 6.8%, while CRISIL maintains its estimated 6.5%, reflecting sustained momentum in private consumption and investment activity.
The Central Bank's monetary policy remains supportive of growth, with the RBI having delivered 3 rate cuts of cumulatively totaling to 100 bps during calendar year, bringing the repo rate to 5.5%.
Margins & costs: Inflation figures for September 2025 came in at 1.54%, the lowest since June 2017, which is reflected in the RBI's CPI inflation forecast, easing to 2.6% for FY '26 from 3.1% previously, driven by GST, rate rationalization and easing commodity prices.
The company's weighted average cost of borrowing declined from 10.8% in Q2 FY '25 to 10.2% in Q2 FY '26, marking a reduction of 60 basis points over the past year.

This declining trend should continue as our incremental borrowing cost is now around 9%-9.25%, supported by improving credit profile, strong lender confidence, and access to more competitive borrowing sources.
